x.around: On the main road out to the airport they really put their foot down. It is however a good well sealed road, nice views over Kigali City and a thrilling ride.

hidden.d: Memorial to 10 Belgian peacekeepers were gunned down on the first day of the 1994 genocide crisis while attempting to protect the Rwandan Prime Minister.
This memorial is the site of four tiled-over mass graves holding the remains of thousands of Tutsis who were executed after the regiment of UN guards protecting them were killed.
Here you can take guided walking tours, cooking classes, or have lunch at an enterprise geared toward enabling women to succeed with computers, literacy, sewing and handicrafts.

x.intro: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda. The centre of political and commercial life, Kigali dominates Rwanda and few visit the country without passing through. The city is developing fast, and is very much a showpiece capital designed to impress visitors from tourists to foreign investors and visiting dignitaries.

must.d: Opened in April 2004 on the 10th anniversary of the genocides. Over 250,000 people are buried here, and there is a truly touching museum. Kigali houses several memorials, museums, and centers dedicated to the Rwandan Genocide.

n.es: Centro Conmemorativo del Genocidio de Kigali
n.fr: Mémorial du Génocide de Kigali – Gisozi

must.d: Natural history museum focusing on Rwanda flora and fauna in the former home of a German named Richard Kandt. Also excellent venue from which to view the city skyline.

n.es: Casa Museo de Historia Natural Kandt

must.d: The abode of the former President Habyarimana, who died in that infamous plane crash of 1994 that sparked the genocide. Guided tours are mandatory, where you can get a glimpse of life as an African dictator in the 1970s & 80s.
Displays of artwork from around Rwanda.

This museum is a collection of the history of the campaign against genocide in the whole country as a summary. It has a map that indicates the basements of all battalions of RPA soldiers and all the routes they took during the…

n.es: Museo de la Campaña contra el Genocidio
n.fr: Mémorial du Musée de la Campagne du Génocide

next.d: home of the mountain gorillas, and the setting for Gorillas in the Mist author Dian Fossey's research. If you can afford it it's an excellent experience... even possible as a daytrip from Kigali.

x.safe: Kigali is relatively safe and friendly as far as African capitals go. Keep your eyes open and your wallet out of the reach of pickpockets, especially in crowded areas. Avoid walking after dark if possible, especially alone. Take extra precaution in the area between New Cadilac Nightclub and Carwash bar.

x.intro: Gicumbi (formerly Byumba) is a district in Northern Province of Rwanda. Gicumbi is one of five districts of Northern Province used to be called Byumba Province. Gicumbi covers 829 lm2 Gicumbi is located in the east of the Northern Province, the northern side of Gicumbi borders with the Republic of Uganda and Burera District, the eastern side of Gicumbi there is Nyagatare and Gatsibo, the western part there is Rurindo District, the southern of Gicumbi there is Gasabo of…

x.around: Taxi-moto (motorbike taxis) are the main form of transport within Cyangugu (and between Cyangugu and Kamembe).
x.intro: Cyangugu is a city of about 64,000 people (2015) in Rusizi District in Western Province of Rwanda.

x.around: Gisenyi is a small town and can easily be gotten around on foot, alternatively there are hundreds of Motorbike Taxis around.
x.intro: Gisenyi is a city in Rubavu district, is the third largest city of Rwanda.

x.around: Butare has plenty of taxis, motorcycle taxis, and bicycle taxis, all of which will be eager to serve you. Also, you can walk from the northernmost part of Butare (the bus station) to the southernmost (the University of Rwanda) in about 20 minutes. (The taxis exist mainly to take Rwandans to their homes farther outside the city.)
x.intro: Butare, also known as Huye, is the third largest city of Rwanda, located in the south.

must.d: Nyanza is a small town with a market, and a few hotels. Main attraction in the Museum of the Kings Palace. Entrance FRw 6000, including a personal guide.
Although a stroll through the University would take at most 20 minutes, it is a worthwhile trip to see an active African university.

In 1994, Murambi was the site of a large massacre at a vocational school where several hundred Tutsis were hiding. It was turned into one of the most compelling and graphic genocide memorials with preserved bodies on display.

n.es: Centro de la memoria del genocidio Murambi
n.it: Centro commemorativo del genocidio di Murambi

must.d: The National Museum is a surprisingly comprehensive and interesting museum. Even travellers knowledgeable about recent Rwandan history will learn much about Rwanda's colonial and post-colonial governments, as well as the Tutsi…

x.around: Kibeho has several motorcycle taxis, but the town could be walked from north to south in 20 minutes, and is generally quite small so they may not be necessary.
x.intro: Kibeho is the largest town in Nyaruguru District, Rwanda, located in the south. The town is famous in central Africa as the location where groups of young men and women had visions of the virgin Mary in the 1980s. One of the few Vatican-approved instances of a sighting of Mary, the town has become a very popular destination during the Assumption of Mary on August 15, when the normally small and tranquil village triples or quadruples in size as people come from neighboring…

x.around: Kibungo is a small town, so you can walk to most places. The urban town center is highly compact and easy to explore. * Motorcycle Taxis (Motos): The absolute king of public transit in Rwanda. Licensed drivers wearing numbered green or red vests wait continuously at the main taxi park and hotel gates to ferry passengers anywhere across the city ridges for a highly budget-friendly fare.

hidden.d: A sprawling, high-energy community trading hub. It offers an incredible look into local commerce, featuring massive open-air columns trading fresh bananas, local textiles, hand-woven baskets, and regional farm produce.

x.intro: Kibungo is a city of 46,000 people (2014) in eastern Rwanda, 100 km from Kigali, along the main road to Tanzania. Kibungo is a major commercial city and the administrative headquarters of the Ngoma District, situated in the Eastern Province of Rwanda. Located approximately 100 kilometers southeast of the national capital, Kigali, it stands as home to roughly 46,000 residents.

x.around: Walking or taking a moto (motorcycle or scooter) are your options.

hidden.d: Since 2023, it's one of four memorials making up the Memorial sites of the Genocide: Nyamata, Murambi, Gisozi and Bisesero.

x.intro: Kibuye is a city in western Rwanda on the shore of Lake Kivu — the surrounding area offers some stunning views of the lake. The new name is Karongi, most people still call it Kibuye though.

intro: Rwanda is an East African country known as the land of a thousand hills. It is easily accessible from Kenya and Uganda, and is one of the safest and most organised countries on the continent. The rolling green highlands, volcanic mountains, and ancient rainforests make it a striking destination.

other.d: The park is home to the 'Big 5' - lion, black rhino, buffalo, elephant, and leopard.

x.around: You can rent a car in Kigali and make the 2 hour drive to the park yourself. If you are staying at a lodge in the park, game drives and walking safaris are offered as part of your stay.
x.intro: Akagera National Park is in the northeast of Rwanda measuring over 1,200 square km. After being decimated by high levels of poaching following the return of refugees and farmers after the 1994 Genocide, the park has been revived and is now the only 'Big 5' reserve in the country. Its inspiring conservation journey has seen the reintroduction of black rhinos in 2017, lions in 2015, and other game animals over the years.
x.safe: Rwanda prides itself on being one of the safest countries in Africa. Crime levels are low, however visitors should take normal safety precautions.

other.d: Home to the mountain gorillas, this park spreads into Uganda and Democratic Republic of the Congo. The setting for Gorillas in the Mist, author Dian Fossey's research.

x.around: If you prefer to self-drive, a 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Most rental car companies operating in Rwanda will not allow non-4WD vehicles to be driven into the national parks, because of the risk of damage on poor roads.
x.intro: Not to be confused with Hawaii Volcanoes National Park in Hawaii. Volcanoes National Park is an extraordinary park in Rwanda, full of impressive tropical rainforest and volcanic scenery, trekking, and is perhaps the best place in the world to see the rare mountain gorillas.
x.safe: Park guides (some of whom are armed) will accompany you on all treks into the park. As a result, there are effectively no safety concerns, provided you follow the instructions of the park guides, and come prepared with appropriate clothing and adequate drinking water.

other.d: The best preserved rainforest in the mountains throughout Central Africa.

x.around: Other than the main road through the forest there are no (public) roads or vehicle tracks in the park, everything is on foot (see do).
x.intro: Nyungwe National Park is in Rwanda, and since 2023 a . It is probably the best preserved rainforest in the mountains throughout Central Africa. The park contains 13 primate species (25% of Africa's total), 275 bird species, 1068 plant species, 85 mammal species, 32 amphibian and 38 reptile species. Many of these animals are restricted-range species that are only found in the Albertine Rift montane forests ecoregion in Africa.
